title: Sobolo
description: Dried hibiscus steeped with ginger, spice, and pineapple skin, then left overnight and sweetened cold. Deep red, properly tart, and served in a jug with far too much ice.
notes: Sweeten it cold, never hot. Sugar reads weaker in a hot pan and you will overshoot every single time.

steps.text: Rinse the dried hibiscus in cold water and pick out any stalks or grit.
Bring the water to a boil with the ginger, cinnamon stick, cloves, and the scrubbed pineapple skin.
steps.tip: The pineapple skin is not a garnish. It carries most of the sweetness the drink has before any sugar goes in.

steps.text: Take the pan off the heat, tip in the hibiscus, cover it, and let it steep until the colour is opaque.
Strain into a jug and refrigerate overnight so it settles and the flavour deepens.
Sweeten the cold drink with the sugar a spoonful at a time, then sharpen it with the lime juice until it makes you wince slightly.
Serve over more ice than seems reasonable — it is meant to dilute as you drink it.
